# deed_entity (Resource)

An entity in the Deed catalog, **declared through the provider's source** (`terraform` by default, see the provider's `source_name` argument).

Deed merges the facets of every source that knows an entity — declarations, importers, runtime observations and UI annotations — into an effective view. This resource manages only the provider's own declaration: its state is read from `GET /entities/{id}/declarations/{source}` and never from the merged view, so values contributed by other sources (and observed health or freshness) never cause a diff. Destroying the resource removes only this declaration; the entity survives while other sources still contribute to it. Read the effective view with the `deed_entity` data source.

If the entity already exists because another source reported it, creating the resource adopts it (the declaration is added). If the provider's source already declares it — for example from another Terraform configuration — the apply fails and asks you to `terraform import` it instead.

Entities cannot be renamed through Terraform: changing `name`, `kind` or `project` replaces the declaration.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "deed_entity" "nas" {
  project = deed_project.homelab.name
  kind    = "server"
  name    = "nas-01"

  display_name    = "NAS"
  description     = "Primary network storage."
  environment     = "homelab"
  owner           = "platform" # a group entity name or ID
  lifecycle_stage = "active"
  icon            = "tabler:server"

  labels = {
    tier = "storage"
  }
  annotations = {
    "example.com/rack" = "rack-1, unit 4"
  }
  links = [
    { type = "dashboard", title = "Grafana", url = "https://grafana.example.com/d/nas-01" },
    { type = "runbook", url = "https://docs.example.com/runbooks/nas-01" },
  ]
  tags = ["storage", "backup-target"]

  version_declared = "7.2.1"
  version_channel  = "stable"

  # Kind-specific properties, validated by Deed against the kind's JSON Schema.
  spec = jsonencode({
    hostname  = "nas-01.home.example.com"
    ipv4      = "192.168.10.20"
    cpu_cores = 4
    memory_mb = 16384
  })

  timeouts = {
    create = "2m"
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `kind` (String) Kind, built-in (`server`, `service`, `repository`, …) or custom (`deed_kind`). Changing it forces a new resource.
- `name` (String) Entity name, unique per project and kind: a lowercase slug (a-z, 0-9, '.', '_', '-'). Changing it forces a new resource.
- `project` (String) Project name or ID. Changing it forces a new resource (the same project by name or ID does not). Import records the project name.

### Optional

- `annotations` (Map of String) Annotations (at most 64; values up to 4096 bytes): free-form notes that are not used for filtering.
- `description` (String) Description (Markdown).
- `display_name` (String) Human-friendly name.
- `environment` (String) Environment slug, e.g. `production` or `homelab`.
- `icon` (String) Icon as `pack:name` (`tabler`, `simple-icons`, `thesvg` or `custom`), e.g. `simple-icons:proxmox`.
- `labels` (Map of String) Labels (at most 64; values up to 256 bytes) used for filtering and grouping. Keys that look like secrets are refused by Deed.
- `lifecycle_stage` (String) Lifecycle stage: `planned`, `active`, `deprecated` or `retired`.
- `links` (Attributes List) Typed external links (at most 32), e.g. the repository, a dashboard or the runbook. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--links))
- `owner` (String) Owning group: a `group` entity ID or name.
- `spec` (String) Kind-specific properties as a JSON object string (use `jsonencode`). Deed validates it server-side against the kind's storage schema (JSON Schema 2020-12), so the provider does not model custom-kind properties as attributes. Deed stores the document re-encoded (sorted keys, compact); the value is compared semantically, so that never causes a diff (reformatting the document in the configuration shows one in-place update that changes nothing in Deed). Values whose keys look like secrets must be secret references (`{ secretRef = { store = "vault", key = "…" } }`).
- `tags` (Set of String) Tags (at most 64, each 1–64 bytes).
- `timeouts` (Attributes) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--timeouts))
- `version_channel` (String) Release channel, e.g. `stable`.
- `version_declared` (String) Declared version of the software, e.g. `1.27.3`.
- `version_policy` (String) Version policy, e.g. `pinned` or `latest-minor`.
- `version_product` (String) Product the version refers to (for upstream release tracking).

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Entity ID (`ent_…`).
- `project_id` (String) Project ID (`prj_…`).

<a id="nestedatt--links"></a>
### Nested Schema for `links`

Required:

- `type` (String) `repository`, `dashboard`, `logs`, `docs`, `runbook`, `metrics`, `alerts`, `ticket` or `other`.
- `url` (String) Absolute `https://` URL (`http://` only when the project allows http links).

Optional:

- `title` (String) Link title.


<a id="nestedatt--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `create` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).
- `delete` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours). Setting a timeout for a Delete operation is only applicable if changes are saved into state before the destroy operation occurs.
- `read` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours). Read operations occur during any refresh or planning operation when refresh is enabled.
- `update` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# By entity ID …
terraform import deed_entity.nas ent_01m5qxagfserct3h3garhw4k71

# … or by natural key: <project>/<kind>/<name> (the kind may contain a slash, e.g. homelab/example.com/ups/ups-01).
terraform import deed_entity.nas homelab/server/nas-01
```
